text:
elaine: seeing a ~40% throughput drop on us-east GPU pool starting ~10:10 UTC, lots of worker restarts and some CUDA OOM traces in logs
infra-bot: alert: tiered-gpu-pool us-east - 10:12 UTC - increased error rate, 23 restarts in 6m :rotating_light:
elaine: stack traces show OOMs during KV cache restores, also a spike in small-allocation failures
sam: grabbed perf traces from two affected workers, pushing to s3: s3://redwood-perf/1908123456/trace.tar.gz
sam: quick diff of allocator histograms -> heavy growth in 256B-2KB slab churn, overall free pages dropping steadily
sam: kernel-selection log shows recent rollout of heuristic v3 (commit cf12b) which prefers fused attention kernels for short sequences
elaine: v3 was rolled 03:00 UTC last night to improve latency for short-chat tails
ryan: does fused attention increase KV footprint or temporary workspace? we saw this before with small-batch bursts
nisha: checked metrics: prefix cache hit rate briefly drops at the same window, causing more KV restore ops per request -> more transient allocations
ops-bot: deploy-bot: roll-forward: reverting kernel-heuristic v3 -> v2 (cf11a) started by @ryan at 10:18 UTC
elaine: after rollback we saw immediate reduction in OOM traces on the rolled hosts, throughput recovering but not fully back to baseline
sam: profile snapshots before/after rollback attached: important bits:
```
# before rollback (fused kernels)
GPU mem used by KV restores: 4.6GB avg
peak transient workspace allocations: 1.2GB
worker restart rate: 3.8/min

# after rollback (non-fused)
GPU mem used by KV restores: 2.7GB avg
peak transient workspace allocations: 0.45GB
worker restart rate: 0.6/min
```

nisha: batching heuristics also contributed — small requests were being coalesced into larger fused kernels which allocate bigger temporary buffers; under fragmentation those buffers failed and triggered OOM cascades
ryan: we drained the most-affected nodes and forced a full KV cache purge + warm-up on healthy hosts to rebalance load
elaine: immediate mitigation notes: 1) rollback kernel-heuristic v3 2) reduce max auto-batch window from 50ms -> 30ms for this pool 3) temporarily increase eviction aggressiveness for KV cache to cap memory per worker
sam: added a flamegraph link (internal): https://perf.redwood/intern/1908123456/flame.html - shows allocation hot path in fused_attention::alloc_workspace
ops-bot: k8s: cordon/drain applied to nodes: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-19 at 10:14 UTC
infra-bot: observed a noisy-tenant pattern on gpu-node-19: one tenant sent many short-seq batched requests between 10:08-10:11 UTC, correlates with spike
isha: follow-up items (P1/P2):
- P1: add slab-fragmentation metric and alert (owner: sam)
- P1: add KV restore transient allocation gauge per-worker (owner: nisha)
- P2: evaluate alternate fused kernel that uses streaming workspace (owner: eng-runtime)
ryan: we should also add an experiment to throttle per-tenant batch concurrency to avoid noisy-tenant blasts
elaine: retrospective: kernel heuristics need a memory-safety check (reject heuristic if predicted transient alloc > thresh) before rollout; add to rollout checklist
sam: performance regression cause summary: fused-kernel heuristic + increased coalescing of small requests -> larger transient workspace allocations -> under fragmented GPU allocator caused CUDA OOM -> worker restarts -> throughput drop
elaine: current status: throughput at ~95% baseline after rollback and node drains, no ongoing restarts for 20m, marking incident as mitigated but not resolved
ryan: estimated RCA doc draft in progress, will post link when ready (ETA 4h)
ops-bot: incident-note: mitigations applied: kernel rollback, batching window reduced, node drains, KV eviction tweak
elaine: tagging relevant folks for postmortem: @sam @nisha @ryan @eng-runtime-team :clipboard:
infra-bot: incident closed for active escalations at 10:25 UTC, monitoring for residuals
